sentences.text: Fossils of Bryantolepis include parts of the skull roof, suborbital region, endocranium, and trunk shield.
The type species Bryantolepis brachycephala was described by Bryant in 1932.
Bryantolepis brachycephala was originally classified in the genus Euryaspis before being reassigned to Bryantolepis.
The species Bryantolepis williamsi was described and named in 2010.
The species name williamsi honors the paleontologist Michael E. Williams.
Bryantolepis brachycephala is one of the most common fish species found in the Beartooth Butte Formation.
Bryantolepis williamsi was found at the Utah-Idaho border in the Grassy Flat Member of the Water Canyon Formation.
Bryantolepis belongs to the family Actinolepididae.
Bryantolepis is classified in the class Placodermi.
Bryantolepis lived during the Early Devonian period.
Bryantolepis lived between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago during the Emsian stage.
